title: Borewell Restoration — Nandur Cluster
summary: Restoring 22 failed borewells and handing maintenance to elected village water committees.
description: Fourteen settlements in the Nandur cluster lost their drinking water source over five years as water tables fell and maintenance funds were never set aside. This project rehabilitates each failed borewell, installs solar pumping where load calculations justify it, and registers a village water committee with a written maintenance budget before any equipment is handed over. A six-month monitoring window then tracks yield, water quality and fee collection.
objectives: Restore 22 failed borewells to working order
Form and register a water committee per settlement
Install flow meters and publish monthly usage data
Train 66 committee members in basic maintenance
outcomes: 14 of 22 borewells restored and handed over
11 water committees constituted with bank accounts
Average collection time for water fell from 4 hours to 40 minutes

title: Rainwater Harvesting in 40 Schools
summary: Recharge pits and storage tanks that carry 40 government schools through the dry months.
description: Each of the 40 schools receives a recharge pit, a first-flush diverter and a storage tank sized to the roof area. Students are taught to read the level gauge and record it weekly, so the infrastructure doubles as a practical science lesson.
objectives: Build recharge and storage at 40 schools
outcomes: 31 schools commissioned
Dry-month drinking water shortfall eliminated at 24 schools

title: Mother's Nutrition Circles
summary: Weekly circles for expectant and new mothers, run by trained community health workers.
description: A twelve-month cycle of weekly meetings covering antenatal care, anaemia screening, breastfeeding and infant feeding. Each circle is led by a community health worker from the same settlement, with a shared growth chart that families keep.
objectives: Refer and follow up high-risk pregnancies within 48 hours
outcomes: 31 circles running with 92% weekly attendance
Antenatal visit coverage up from 54% to 81%

title: Mobile Health Camps
summary: A fortnightly clinic-on-wheels covering settlements more than 15 km from a PHC.
description: A van equipped for screening, first-line treatment and referrals visits eight settlements on a fixed fortnightly rotation, staffed by a doctor, a nurse and a counsellor. Registration is done on paper and entered the same day, so follow-up lists are never lost.
objectives: Screen for hypertension and diabetes at every camp
Close the referral loop within 14 days
outcomes: 106 camps held
1,840 referrals completed against 2,010 issued

title: Kitchen Garden Collectives
summary: 600 household gardens that supply both the plate and a weekly market stall.
description: Households receive seed kits, drip lines and three sessions on seasonal planting. Surplus is pooled into a collective stall, with a written price list agreed at the start of each week.
objectives: Cut household spend on vegetables by a quarter
outcomes: 426 gardens established
9 collectives selling weekly with published price lists

title: Farmer Producer Group Scale-up
summary: Taking a 140-member FPO from one crop to four with transparent procurement records.
description: The producer group is supported to add processing, a shared cold store and four crops under a single set of books. Every purchase and payout is posted on a board at the collection centre as well as in the group's ledger.

title: After-School Learning Centres
summary: 30 remedial centres that take children from reading below grade level to at grade.
description: Two hours each evening in a community room, grouped by reading level rather than age, using a shared assessment rubric. Facilitators are drawn from the settlement and paid from the project's own budget.
objectives: Assess every child at entry and every quarter
Bring 70% of participants to grade-level reading
outcomes: 24 centres open with 1,180 children enrolled
61% of participants reached grade-level reading in two quarters

title: Library Corners in 60 Schools
summary: Curated shelves, a lending register and a student librarian in every partner school.
description: Each school gets roughly 300 titles chosen with teachers, a lending register kept by trained student librarians, and a quarterly review of which books are actually borrowed.
objectives: Track borrowings for two full academic years
outcomes: All 60 corners established
Average borrowings rose from 4 to 19 per child per term

title: Incremental Housing Upgrades
summary: Owner-driven roof, wall and sanitation upgrades in 250 homes.
description: Households choose which of three upgrade packages to take, buy materials through a shared rate contract, and record every receipt on a wall-mounted ledger that the project audits monthly.
objectives: Keep material costs within the published rate contract
outcomes: 85 upgrades completed before the work paused
Material costs held 11% under the rate contract

title: Ridge-to-Valley Watershed Treatment
summary: Trenches, bunds and check dams across 900 hectares of degraded ridge land.
description: Continuous contour trenching on the ridge, farm ponds below it and three check dams in the valley, all executed by the farming households who will use them, with satellite-based cover reporting published each season.
objectives: Build 3 check dams and 240 farm ponds
outcomes: 412 hectares treated
Two check dams commissioned and holding through the monsoon

title: Cyclone Preparedness Network
summary: Volunteer wardens, loudspeakers and rehearsed evacuation routes in 26 coastal wards.
description: Each ward gets a trained volunteer warden, a tested loudspeaker chain and a marked evacuation route rehearsed twice a year. Warning messages are issued in the local language and confirmed by call-back before an evacuation is called.
outcomes: 78 wardens trained
Call-back confirmation at 94% across two warning cycles

title: Public Sanitation Blocks at Market Yards
summary: Six user-charged toilet blocks at district market yards, with published cleaning rotas.
description: Each block is built to a common design, operated by a self-help group on a published tariff, and cleaned on a rota that is posted at the entrance with the inspector's signature.
objectives: Hand each to a self-help group
outcomes: All 6 blocks operational
Average daily usage of 410 people across the six sites
